name: The Arrangement
description: A corporate-sponsored neural-feed dating competition in which twelve Tier 3 and Tier 4 contestants compete for a legally binding five-year companionship contract with a Spire-level executive whose identity is concealed until the finale. Contestants live each episode in full sensory immersion, experiencing manufactured intimacy scenarios that blur the line between genuine emotion and engineered neural response. The show was enormously popular and genuinely disturbing to watch, and nobody could stop.
cultural_impact: The Arrangement sparked the first mainstream public conversation about consent and neural manipulation in immersive entertainment, though it changed nothing legislatively.
story_hooks: A contestant from Season 3 claims their post-show personality is not their own — they want someone to prove the feed was used for non-consensual behavioral conditioning.
The concealed executive at the center of Season 5 has gone missing before the finale; the production company needs the finale to air regardless.
A Tier 2 street medic begins treating patients with identical neurological symptoms — all of them recent viewers of The Arrangement.
